section_summary: This section chiefly concerns State, Commerce, and military processing of applications for entry into occupied Japan by business representatives, diplomats, missionaries, and other foreign travelers. It includes applications, clearances, extensions, returned permits, passport and exit-document arrangements, and notifications to overseas posts. Notable cases include the Philippine Ambassador’s party, Ezra K. Zilkha, Ho Shun Ying, Walter and Lizzi Spitzer, Yoshitaro Suzuki, and several Iranian traders.

subfiles.title: Application of Raghbir Singh Narula to visit Japan or Korea
subfiles.to: U.S. Departments of Commerce and State; SCAP
subfiles.about: Narula requests travel permission to investigate purchasing unfinished Japanese cotton cloth.
subfiles.summary: Narula proposes buying unfinished cotton cloth for processing in the United States and re-export.

subfiles.title: Return of passport for Victor Kelly Bashi
subfiles.from: A. Shebairo, Occident & Orient Products Inc.
subfiles.about: The company returns Victor Kelly Bashi's passport as requested.
subfiles.summary: Occident & Orient Products returns Bashi's passport to the State Department.

subfiles.title: Return of unused military permit for V. Kelly Bashi
subfiles.about: Protective Services returns Bashi's unused April 29 military permit.
subfiles.summary: Bashi obtained later entry permission and returned his unused military permit for Army disposition.

subfiles.title: Telegram concerning the Kurbangali sisters' repatriation
subfiles.about: Najiy and Anisa Kurbangali report Soviet documentation requirements for departure on a repatriation ship.
subfiles.summary: The sisters need birth certificates and are advised also to obtain passports before repatriation.

subfiles.title: Commerce memorandum and list of approved Japan and Korea travelers
subfiles.about: Commerce forwards applicants approved for business travel, subject to military approval.
subfiles.summary: The list identifies representatives, firms, citizenship, locations, requested entry dates, and travel modes for Japan and Korea.

subfiles.title: Telephone memorandum concerning Ezra K. Zilkha's permit
subfiles.about: Mellor informs Zilkha that his Japan military permit has arrived.
subfiles.summary: Zilkha accepts the September 23–October 23 entry period and requests immediate delivery.

subfiles.title: Letter transmitting Ezra K. Zilkha's military permit
subfiles.about: Chappell sends Zilkha's Japan permit and requests final travel details.
subfiles.summary: The enclosed permit authorizes entry through October 23 and a sixty-day stay.

subfiles.title: Request for renewed Japan clearance for John M. Bowes
subfiles.about: Protective Services forwards Bowes's renewed application after he could not use his earlier clearance.
subfiles.summary: The Army is asked to submit Bowes's unchanged application to SCAP for the earliest possible entry.

subfiles.title: Manila telegram requesting Japan entry for John M. Bowes
subfiles.about: The Embassy requests renewed authority for Bowes to travel to Japan for purchasing.
subfiles.summary: Canadian trader Bowes seeks a two-week visit to buy cement, construction materials, chinaware, and toys.

subfiles.title: Envelope from American Nile Corporation
subfiles.about: Mailing envelope for Ezra K. Zilkha's September 23 letter.
subfiles.summary: Envelope addressed to Chappell at the Department of State.

subfiles.title: Ezra K. Zilkha letter concerning exit and re-entry permits
subfiles.about: Zilkha asks for help obtaining departure authority before his planned Japan trip.
subfiles.summary: Zilkha plans October 6 air travel via San Francisco and seeks expedited exit and re-entry documentation.

subfiles.title: Application of Ezra K. Zilkha to visit Japan
subfiles.from: Ezra K. Zilkha; American Nile Corporation
subfiles.to: U.S. Departments of Commerce and State; SCAP
subfiles.about: Zilkha applies to purchase Japanese gray piece goods for export markets.
subfiles.summary: Zilkha seeks a sixty-day buying visit to Tokyo, Osaka, and Kobe.

subfiles.title: Commerce cover memorandum on Ho Shun Ying's extension
subfiles.about: Commerce forwards Albert Lee Company's request to extend Ho Shun Ying's Japan authorization.
subfiles.summary: The firm requests validity through October because passport issuance delayed Ho's travel.

subfiles.title: Albert Lee Company request concerning Ho Shun Ying
subfiles.from: Hu Hsiang Chu, Albert Lee Company
subfiles.about: The firm asks Commerce to extend Ho Shun Ying's SCAP permission through October.
subfiles.summary: Chinese passport processing requires another month, preventing use of the existing authorization.

subfiles.title: Commerce Department envelope to Leonelda Mellor
subfiles.about: Official envelope carrying Commerce correspondence to Protective Services.
subfiles.summary: Official-business envelope addressed to Mellor at the State Department.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Albert Lee Company letter concerning Ho Shun Ying
subfiles.from: Hu Hsiang Chu, Albert Lee Company
subfiles.about: A duplicate copy requests extension of Ho Shun Ying's entry permission.
subfiles.summary: Passport delays prompt a request to extend Ho's SCAP authorization through October.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Tokyo concerning Yoshitaro Suzuki
subfiles.to: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: State reports Brazil's authorization for Suzuki's permanent immigration and requests military consideration of an exit permit.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo is asked to inform occupation authorities and consider Suzuki's departure, while noting his family's 1942 repatriation to Japan.

subfiles.title: Memorandum to the Brazilian Embassy concerning Yoshitaro Suzuki
subfiles.about: State explains SCAP's required travel-document procedure for a Japanese national immigrating permanently.
subfiles.summary: Brazil should provide Suzuki a travel document through its protecting power's representative in Tokyo, who may then seek his exit permit. State is separately alerting the occupation authorities.

subfiles.title: Telegram to Manila announcing Harry Flitterman's clearance
subfiles.about: State announces Flitterman's authorization to enter Japan between October 15 and November 15.
subfiles.summary: Flitterman receives a sixty-day clearance and must carry passport photographs and a certified telegram copy.

subfiles.title: Blank Department of State records charge sheet
subfiles.about: Blank form for charging a document from State Department files.
subfiles.summary: Uncompleted records charge sheet listing document-type options.

subfiles.title: Notification to Surplus Corporation of Flitterman's clearance
subfiles.about: Chappell reports Flitterman's authorized Japan entry period and sixty-day stay.
subfiles.summary: The company is told that the Embassy in Manila has also been notified.

subfiles.title: Return of Harry Flitterman's military permit to the Army
subfiles.about: Chappell returns Flitterman's military permit after notifying the Embassy in Manila.
subfiles.summary: Military permit 10368 is returned to the Army after overseas notification.

subfiles.title: Application of Harry Flitterman to visit Japan
subfiles.from: Harry Flitterman; Surplus Corporation of America
subfiles.to: U.S. Departments of Commerce and State; SCAP
subfiles.about: Flitterman applies for a business visit concerning manufacture of blankets from American woolen rags.
subfiles.summary: He proposes visiting Tokyo, Osaka, and Hiroshima for approximately four months.

subfiles.title: Bank reference for Harry Flitterman and Surplus Corporation
subfiles.from: F. B. Danby, Union Bank & Trust Company
subfiles.about: The bank supplies a favorable confidential credit reference for the company and David Flitterman.
subfiles.summary: The company has maintained satisfactory accounts, repaid unsecured credit, and is considered financially responsible.

subfiles.title: Envelope from Naess, Mejlaender & Company
subfiles.about: Registered-mail envelope for Erling D. Naess's returned military permit.
subfiles.summary: Registered envelope addressed to Chappell at the State Department.

subfiles.title: Erling D. Naess letter returning an unused permit
subfiles.about: Naess returns his expired Japan military permit after negotiation delays prevented travel.
subfiles.summary: Unforeseen SCAP negotiations made it impossible to use permit 9613 within its validity period.

subfiles.title: State Department return of Erling D. Naess's permit to the Army
subfiles.about: Protective Services returns Naess's unused military permit to the Military Permit Section.
subfiles.summary: Naess could not travel because negotiations with SCAP were delayed.

subfiles.title: London despatch transmitting the Spitzers' application
subfiles.about: The Embassy transmits Walter and Lizzi Spitzer's application for entry into Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Austrian couple seeks military permission to enter Japan.

subfiles.title: Application of Walter and Lizzi Spitzer to enter Japan
subfiles.about: The Spitzers seek permanent residence in Japan after years in China and Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: Their application records Austrian nationality, Asian residence, proposed routes, employment, passports, and permanent settlement in Kobe.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of the Spitzers' application to the Army
subfiles.about: Protective Services asks the Army to submit the Spitzers' application to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: A memorandum of approval would suffice instead of issuing physical military permits.

subfiles.title: Instruction to London on British processing of Walter Spitzer's application
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission London
subfiles.about: State explains that Spitzer's application must proceed through British trade channels.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo declined normal consideration because Spitzer represented a British firm unknown to the United Kingdom Liaison Mission.

subfiles.title: Military clearance memorandum for Ho Shun Ying
subfiles.about: The Army clears Ho Shun Ying to enter Japan during October.
subfiles.summary: Ho receives a sixty-day stay and must carry two passport photographs.

subfiles.title: E. G. Homrighausen request for action on his Japan application
subfiles.about: Homrighausen urgently requests a decision on his proposed November missionary visit to Japan.
subfiles.summary: He plans to visit Presbyterian missionaries and Japanese ministers near Tokyo and supplies several prominent references.

subfiles.title: Envelope from Occident & Orient Products
subfiles.about: Envelope for correspondence concerning Victor Kelly Bashi.
subfiles.summary: Company envelope addressed to the State Department.

subfiles.title: Cancellation request for Victor Kelly Bashi's entry authority
subfiles.from: A. Shebairo, Occident & Orient Products Inc.
subfiles.about: The company reports that Bashi is no longer employed and asks that his permit be voided.
subfiles.summary: Authorities are asked to cancel Bashi's authority to travel from Bangkok to Japan.

subfiles.title: Airgram to Bangkok concerning Victor Kelly Bashi
subfiles.about: State relays the former employer's request that Bashi's Japan entry authority be treated as void.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy is informed that Occident & Orient Products no longer sponsors Bashi.

subfiles.title: Notification to the Army concerning Victor Kelly Bashi
subfiles.about: State forwards the employer's cancellation letter and reports notifications to Bangkok and Commerce.
subfiles.summary: Bashi's former employer has withdrawn responsibility for his September Japan permit.

subfiles.title: Tehran despatch transmitting Hassan Nader-Esphahani's application
subfiles.from: Randall S. Williams, American Embassy Tehran
subfiles.about: The Embassy submits an Iranian trader's application for entry into Japan.
subfiles.summary: Nader-Esphahani seeks to buy chinaware, glassware, and haberdashery in December or January.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Hassan Nader-Esphahani's application to the Army
subfiles.about: Protective Services asks the Army to submit Nader-Esphahani's application to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: A memorandum of approval is requested instead of a physical military permit.

subfiles.title: Military clearance memorandum for John M. Bowes
subfiles.about: The Army clears Bowes to enter Japan from September 30 through October 30.
subfiles.summary: Bowes receives a sixty-day stay as Green & Loveless Company's representative.

subfiles.title: Telegram to Manila announcing John M. Bowes's clearance
subfiles.about: State announces Bowes's Japan entry clearance and documentation requirements.
subfiles.summary: Bowes may enter through October 30, remain sixty days, and carry two passport photographs.

subfiles.title: Telegram to Hong Kong announcing Ho Shun Ying's clearance
subfiles.about: State announces Ho Shun Ying's October entry clearance for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Ho may remain sixty days and must carry two passport photographs.

subfiles.title: File memorandum on Ho Shun Ying's renewed clearance
subfiles.about: Mellor confirms that passport delays caused Ho to miss her earlier clearance.
subfiles.summary: Commerce confirms Albert Lee Company wants Ho's October authorization and will accept telegram charges.

subfiles.title: Philippine Embassy note requesting entry for the Ambassador's party
subfiles.about: The Ambassador requests Japan permits for himself and five Embassy staff members traveling to the Philippines.
subfiles.summary: The six-person party plans Northwest Airlines travel from Washington, arriving in Tokyo October 18 for a ten-day visit. The Embassy offers to reimburse cable expenses.

subfiles.title: Application of Joaquin M. Elizalde to enter Japan
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Joint Chiefs of Staff
subfiles.about: The Philippine Ambassador applies for a ten-day diplomatic visit to Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Elizalde requests entry on October 18 while traveling from the United States.

subfiles.title: Application of Tomas G. de Castro to enter Japan
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Joint Chiefs of Staff
subfiles.about: The Philippine Embassy's First Secretary applies as a member of Elizalde's party.
subfiles.summary: De Castro requests Tokyo entry with the Ambassador's official party.

subfiles.title: Application of Reynaldo Lardizabal Jr. to enter Japan
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Joint Chiefs of Staff
subfiles.about: The Philippine Embassy's Third Secretary applies as a member of Elizalde's party.
subfiles.summary: Lardizabal seeks a ten-day official visit to Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Application of Carmen L. Horton to enter Japan
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Joint Chiefs of Staff
subfiles.about: The Philippine Embassy technical assistant applies as a member of Elizalde's party.
subfiles.summary: Horton seeks a ten-day official visit to Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Application of Trophy Villaroman Ocampo to enter Japan
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Joint Chiefs of Staff
subfiles.about: The Philippine Embassy press assistant applies as a member of Elizalde's party.
subfiles.summary: Ocampo seeks a ten-day official visit to Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Application of Laureano Aberilla to enter Japan
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Joint Chiefs of Staff
subfiles.about: Elizalde's valet applies to accompany the Ambassador's party to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Aberilla requests entry as a member of the Philippine Ambassador's party.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of the Philippine Ambassador's party applications
subfiles.about: State requests urgent military permits for Ambassador Elizalde and his five-person staff party.
subfiles.summary: Six applications are forwarded for immediate attention; Horton's permit may be delivered with the others despite her U.S. citizenship.

subfiles.title: Receipt for six Philippine Embassy military permits
subfiles.about: Receipt records delivery of six numbered Japan military permits.
subfiles.summary: De Castro acknowledges permits for Elizalde and all five accompanying staff members.

subfiles.title: Telephone memorandum on Ezra K. Zilkha's exit-permit waiver
subfiles.about: Mellor informs Finckelstein that Zilkha's exit-permit requirement has been waived.
subfiles.summary: INS will send Zilkha's re-entry permit to San Francisco before his October 9 departure.

subfiles.title: Visa Division waiver for Ezra K. Zilkha
subfiles.about: The form records waiver of Zilkha's exit permit and arrangements for his re-entry permit.
subfiles.summary: Zilkha will depart San Francisco October 9 using military permit 10367.

subfiles.title: Telegram to Tehran announcing Houshang Ansary's clearance
subfiles.about: State announces Ansary's authorization to enter Japan between October 1 and November 1.
subfiles.summary: Ansary may remain sixty days and must carry two passport photographs.

subfiles.title: Envelope from Amerasia Traders
subfiles.about: Envelope for correspondence concerning E. Slutsky's travel.
subfiles.summary: Amerasia Traders envelope addressed to Chappell at the State Department.

subfiles.title: Amerasia Traders letter concerning E. Slutsky's departure
subfiles.about: The firm reports Slutsky's October 13 departure and requests an exit-permit waiver.
subfiles.summary: Slutsky will leave LaGuardia Field on Northwest Airlines using military permit 9375.

subfiles.title: Diplomatic note extending Harry Julius Hurwitz's entry period
subfiles.to: Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Union of South Africa
subfiles.about: State provides Hurwitz a replacement permit after a shipping strike prevented use of his original clearance.
subfiles.summary: Permit 12655 authorizes entry from November 10 through December 10. Hurwitz must report his departure details so exit requirements can be waived.

subfiles.title: File memorandum on Harry Julius Hurwitz's extension
subfiles.about: Mellor records arrangements to extend Hurwitz's Japan entry clearance.
subfiles.summary: Major Larson approves November 10–December 10 validity and agrees to issue a document.

subfiles.title: Military clearance memorandum for Abdul Hossein Naderpour
subfiles.about: The Army clears Naderpour for Japan entry from December 1 through January 1.
subfiles.summary: Naderpour receives a sixty-day stay and must carry two passport photographs.

subfiles.title: Telegram to Tehran announcing Abdul Hossein Naderpour's clearance
subfiles.about: State announces Naderpour's authorization to enter Japan during December.
subfiles.summary: Naderpour may remain sixty days and must carry two passport photographs.

subfiles.title: Envelope from Perret & Berthoud S.A.
subfiles.about: Air-mail envelope for the firm's inquiry about a Japan entry visa.
subfiles.summary: Geneva envelope addressed to the State Department in Washington.

subfiles.title: Perret & Berthoud request for E. L. Bethell's Japan visa
subfiles.about: The Swiss watch firm requests forms or authorization for Bethell's short business visit to Japan.
subfiles.summary: British sales manager Bethell plans a two-to-three-week Japan stop during a wider Far Eastern tour and supplies passport details.
